Ohio Watershed PFAS Contamination Risk Prediction using Machine Learning

By: Kingsley Kanjin, Geospatial Scientist & Water Quality Planner
Key Statistics
Total HUC12 Watersheds
1,541
Watersheds With PFAS
117
PFOA/PFOS Systems
56
Other PFAS Systems
75
Total Detections
665
Priority Unmonitored
14
1
Data — EPA UCMR5 (1.9M records), ECHO (PWS), DoD MIRTA (15 military), TRI (8 PFAS facilities), USGS WBD (1,541 HUC12).
2
Filtering — 34,135 Ohio records → 665 confirmed detections across 141 water systems.
3
Spatial Join — 131 PWS joined to HUC12 (EPSG:26917, predicate = within).
4
Risk Score — 0–100 composite: system count (30%) + detections (30%) + max conc. (25%) + PFOA/PFOS (15%).
5
Features — 9 spatial variables: area, shape, centroid, dist. to PFAS detection, military site, TRI facility.
6
Model — Random Forest 300 trees + SMOTE. 5-fold CV macro F1 = 0.980 ± 0.002.
7
Output — Risk predicted for all 1,539 OH watersheds. 14 unmonitored flagged Moderate+.

Key Findings

▲ NE Ohio — Mahoning Valley. Newton Falls: 0.2200 µg/L — 55× EPA MCL.

▲ SW Ohio — Wright-Patterson AFB AFFF plume affects multiple HUC12 subwatersheds.

14 unmonitored watersheds predicted Moderate+ risk.

Regulatory Context

EPA 2024 PFAS MCLs:
• PFOA & PFOS: 4 ppt
• PFHxS, PFNA, HFPO-DA: 10 ppt
• Compliance: April 2029

56 systems must install GAC or reverse osmosis.

Source Attribution

True source features contribute 17.3% model importance:

• Military sites — 7.4%. Wright-Patterson AFB is key AFFF source.

• TRI facilities — 9.5%. Covestro Newark highest at 260 lbs.

Model Notes

CV F1 = 0.980 ± 0.002 — strong generalization.

Limited by small minority class samples — only 41 Moderate and 6 High risk watersheds observed.

Predictions are screening-level — field verification recommended.
